description:
Found 2026-09-02 while probing fz-kdt.120 (head d2a5f3510). Four lines, no
answer after 60 s on `fz2 interp` and `fz2 run` (Elixir: {2, {1, :start}}):

    fn main() do
      dbg(Enum.reduce([1, 2], :start, fn (x, acc) -> {x, acc} end))
    end

Siblings that answer in well under a second: seed 0 with `acc + 0.5` (1.0),
seed 0 with `acc + x` (3), seed [] with `x` (2). So it is the accumulator
type NESTING ({int, {int, :start}} -> {int, {int, {int, :start}}} ...) that
runs away, and the RETURN_WIDENING_BUDGET (8 strict ascents -> convergence
_class, 16 -> any) is not ending it in time. NOT a job storm: in 60 s the
telemetry holds only 6517 job spans and 3261 work_graph.applied, and the
busiest activation completes 5 times -- the time is inside jobs (1523
canon.type events; a Types operation on the nested tuple looks super-linear),
so the first probe is a per-job span profile (--log-telemetry, longest span)
rather than a wake count. House law: a simple program must answer in
seconds; an unbounded ascent must hit its budget in a bounded number of
rounds AND each round must be cheap on a small program.
title: Enum.reduce with a tuple-nesting accumulator does not terminate: {x, acc} over [1, 2] runs past 60s on interp and JIT
